newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France, Air India in alliance.
newsitem.headline: Air France, Air India in alliance.

text.p: Air France said on Monday it had struck a deal with Air India which would open the way for a strategic alliance between the two airlines.
Air France said in a statement the exclusive deal was finalised on Sunday after two days of talks and was the first of its kind between Europe and India.

The deal will allow Air India to use the Air France hub at Paris airport Charles-de-Gaulle, boost capacity between the two countries, give Air India discounts when using Air France all cargo planes and link the two carriers' frequent fliers programmes.
Air France said chairman Christian Blanc would sign an official agreement in the coming weeks.
U.S. carriers Delta Air Lines and Continental inaugurated an alliance with the French carrier by unveiling registration facilities at Air Frances' Charles de Gaulle hub in April.

Last month Air France executive vice-president and chief operating officer Francois Bachelet said the French carrier was looking to build up a global network of airline alliances to target fast-growing intercontinental markets.
In August last year Indian newspapers quoted Blanc as saying Air France had asked Air-India to join a proposed globabl alliance.
